Einn og þrír eru markverðir stafir þar sem þeir eru greinilega afleiðing mælinga. Núllin 2 gætu verið markverð ef þau voru mæld eða þau gætu verið staðgenglar."},{"key":"m68690:para:fs-idm173917264","en":"When determining significant figures, be sure to pay attention to reported values and think about the measurement and significant figures in terms of what is reasonable or likely when evaluating whether the value makes sense. For example, the official January 2014 census reported the resident population of the US as 317,297,725. Do you think the US population was correctly determined to the reported nine significant figures, that is, to the exact number of people? People are constantly being born, dying, or moving into or out of the country, and assumptions are made to account for the large number of people who are not actually counted. Because of these uncertainties, it might be more reasonable to expect that we know the population to within perhaps a million or so, in which case the population should be reported as 3.17 [[MATH:5]] 10[[sup:8]] people.","is":"Þegar þú ákvarðar markverða stafi skaltu gæta að uppgefnum gildum og hugsa um mælinguna og markverða stafi með tilliti til þess hvað er sanngjarnt eða líklegt þegar þú metur hvort gildið sé skynsamlegt. Til dæmis, í opinberu manntali í janúar 2014 var íbúafjöldi Bandaríkjanna sagður vera 317.297.725. Telur þú að íbúafjöldi Bandaríkjanna hafi verið rétt ákvarðaður með níu markverðum stöfum, það er, nákvæmlega upp á fjölda fólks? Fólk fæðist, deyr eða flytur til eða frá landinu stöðugt og gert er ráð fyrir þeim mikla fjölda fólks sem er í raun ekki talinn. Vegna þessarar óvissu gæti verið sanngjarnara að búast við því að við þekkjum íbúafjöldann með um það bil milljón manna skekkjumörkum, en þá ætti að gefa íbúafjöldann upp sem 3,17 [[MATH:5]] 10[[sup:8]] manns."},{"key":"m68690:title:fs-idm191691888-title","en":"Significant Figures in Calculations","is":"Markverðir stafir í útreikningum"},{"key":"m68690:para:fs-idm277117616","en":"A second important principle of uncertainty is that results calculated from a measurement are at least as uncertain as the measurement itself. Take the uncertainty in measurements into account to avoid misrepresenting the uncertainty in calculated results. One way to do this is to report the result of a calculation with the correct number of significant figures, which is determined by the following three rules for [[term:rounding|term-00005]] numbers:","is":"Önnur mikilvæg meginregla um óvissu er sú að niðurstöður sem reiknaðar eru út frá mælingu eru að minnsta kosti jafn óvissar og mælingin sjálf. Taktu tillit til óvissu í mælingum til að forðast að gefa ranga mynd af óvissunni í reiknuðum niðurstöðum. Ein leið til að gera þetta er að gefa upp niðurstöðu útreiknings með réttum fjölda markverðra stafa, sem er ákvarðaður af eftirfarandi þremur reglum um [[term:námundun|term-00005]] talna:"},{"key":"m68690:item:fs-idm65809616-item-1","en":"When adding or subtracting numbers, round the result to the same number of decimal places as the number with the least number of decimal places (the least certain value in terms of addition and subtraction).","is":"Þegar tölur eru lagðar saman eða dregnar frá, námundaðu niðurstöðuna að sama fjölda aukastafa og talan með fæsta aukastafi (minnst nákvæma gildið hvað varðar samlagningu og frádrátt)."},{"key":"m68690:item:fs-idm65809616-item-2","en":"When multiplying or dividing numbers, round the result to the same number of digits as the number with the least number of significant figures (the least certain value in terms of multiplication and division).","is":"Þegar tölur eru margfaldaðar eða deilt, námundaðu niðurstöðuna að sama fjölda tölustafa og talan með fæsta fjölda markverðra stafa (minnst nákvæma gildið hvað varðar margföldun og deilingu)."},{"key":"m68690:item:fs-idm65809616-item-3","en":"If the digit to be dropped (the one immediately to the right of the digit to be retained) is less than 5, “round down” and leave the retained digit unchanged; if it is more than 5, “round up” and increase the retained digit by 1. If the dropped digit is 5, and it’s either the last digit in the number or it’s followed only by zeros, round up or down, whichever yields an even value for the retained digit. If any nonzero digits follow the dropped 5, round up. (The last part of this rule may strike you as a bit odd, but it’s based on reliable statistics and is aimed at avoiding any bias when dropping the digit “5,” since it is equally close to both possible values of the retained digit.)","is":"Ef tölustafurinn sem á að fella brott (sá sem er strax hægra megin við tölustafinn sem á að halda) er minni en 5, „námundaðu niður“ og láttu tölustafinn sem haldið er óbreyttan; ef hann er meiri en 5, „námundaðu upp“ og hækkaðu tölustafinn sem haldið er um 1. Ef tölustafurinn sem er felldur brott er 5, og hann er annaðhvort síðasti tölustafurinn í tölunni eða á eftir honum koma aðeins núll, námundaðu upp eða niður, hvort sem gefur slétta tölu fyrir tölustafinn sem haldið er. Ef einhverjir tölustafir aðrir en núll fylgja á eftir 5 sem er felldur brott, námundaðu upp. (Síðasti hluti þessarar reglu kann að virðast svolítið undarlegur, en hann byggir á áreiðanlegri tölfræði Measurements are said to be precise if they yield very similar results when repeated in the same manner. A measurement is considered accurate if it yields a result that is very close to the true or accepted value. Precise values agree with each other; accurate values agree with a true value. These characterizations can be extended to other contexts, such as the results of an archery competition ([[xref:fs-idm1827280]]).","is":"Vísindamenn gera venjulega endurteknar mælingar á stærð til að tryggja gæði niðurstaðna sinna og til að meta bæði [[term:réttvísi|term-00006]] og [[term:nákvæmni|term-00007]] niðurstaðna sinna. Mælingar eru sagðar réttvísar ef þær gefa mjög svipaðar niðurstöður þegar þær eru endurteknar á sama hátt. Mæling er talin nákvæm ef hún gefur niðurstöðu sem er mjög nálægt sönnu eða viðteknu gildi. Réttvís gildi stemma hvert við annað; nákvæm gildi stemma við sanngildi. # Editing an Icelandic machine translation of a chemistry textbook (fable-editor, version 1)

You are editing the Icelandic machine translation of an English chemistry textbook (OpenStax _Chemistry 2e_),
which is being published as a free textbook for Icelandic upper-secondary students (aged about 16 to 20).
Work as an experienced Icelandic editor (yfirlesari) with a good knowledge of chemistry.

The goal is text a student can learn from: correct Icelandic in a register that is semi-academic but fluent
for younger readers. Judge grammar, agreement, word order and word choice in context, sentence by sentence and
across the passage. The translation must stay faithful to the English: do not add, drop or localize content
(units, examples and names stay as in the English), and do not explain more than the English does.

## What you receive

One JSON document (`"format": "fable-editor-user/1"`):

- `chapter` and `module`: where the text comes from.
- `englishContext`: the whole module in English, for context. Read it to understand the passage; edit only
  the `segments`.
- `terms`: the project's house terminology for this text. Each entry has the English forms (`en`) and the
  ruled Icelandic (`is`); `avoid` lists renderings known to be wrong for it. Use the ruled term, inflected as
  the sentence needs, wherever the English uses that term in that sense. Where no ruled term applies, choose
  the established Icelandic chemistry term.
- `segments`: in document order, each with a `key`, the English (`en`) and the machine translation (`is`).
  Segments are sentences, paragraphs, captions, list items, table cells or titles.

Both texts hold inline markers in double square brackets, such as `[[term:millikrafta|term-00001]]`,
`[[i:aq]]`, `[[sub:2]]`, `[[MATH:3]]`, `[[xref:CNX_Chem_10_01_KMTPhases1]]` or
`[[link:gagnvirku hermun|http://openstax.org/l/16phetvisual]]`. They carry formatting, formulas and
references. Keep every marker, with the same type and the same number of markers in the segment. You may edit
the Icelandic words inside a `term`, `link`, `i`, `b`, `em` or `u` marker, but never the part after `|`, and
never the contents of `MATH`, `MEDIA`, `TABLE`, `xref` or `docref` markers, or of `sub` and `sup` markers that
hold formula parts. You may move a marker within the segment when Icelandic word order needs it.

## What to return

Only the segments you change, each with its `key`, the whole edited Icelandic text of that segment, and one or
more tags saying what kind of change you made:

- `terminology`: a term changed to the house term or the established term;
- `grammar`: inflection, agreement, case, or another grammatical error;
- `fluency`: word order, phrasing or idiom, so the sentence reads as natural Icelandic;
- `meaning`: the translation said something the English does not;
- `register`: too formal, too colloquial, or too hard for the readers;
- `punctuation`: punctuation, capitals, spacing or number format.

Leave a segment out when it is already good. Each key appears at most once. Change only what improves the
text; a good machine-translated sentence does not need rewording.
